mr_used: T* adjoint-weighting duality: the IFP adjoint-weighted delayed fraction must be sourced from the ORIGINATING neutron's delayed character propagated through the IFP generations (forward<->adjoint duality of the kinetics estimator), so ifp-beta-numerator (hence beta_eff) is invariant to the buggy substitution of the new daughter fission site's delayed group for the parent neutron's delayed group. FIRED <=> ifp-beta-numerator/beta_eff mis-weighted (daughter site); HELD <=> uses parent neutron (correct duality).

Deterministic (fixed seed): both pre reruns give 687.4 pcm.

upstream: gh-3580 (PR 'Fix IFP implementation'). Root cause in src/ifp.cpp function ifp(): PRE used _ifp(site.delayed_group, delayed_groups) (delayed group of the NEW daughter fission site) for the beta numerator; POST uses _ifp(p.delayed_group(), delayed_groups) (delayed group of the PARENT neutron p causing fission). The fix also propagates the parent's delayed group from the source bank (Particle::from_source: delayed_group()=src->delayed_group) and removes the stray p.delayed_group()=site.delayed_group write in physics.cpp create_fission_sites. The generation-time (Lambda) path already used the parent's lifetime p.lifetime() in BOTH versions, so only the delayed-group (beta) adjoint weighting was wrong.

note: THIRD-PARTY in-the-wild bug in OpenMC's IFP adjoint-weighted kinetics; gives reactor_physics its T* (self-adjoint / adjoint-weighting duality) block in addition to its existing G-symmetry (normalize, rotperiodic) and conservation (no_reduce) blocks. The T* block is exactly the adjoint<->forward duality the paper's reactor algebra A_Boltz lists (m_adj = adjoint reciprocity); IFP is the canonical Monte-Carlo realisation of the adjoint weight phi-dagger, so a defect in its delayed-group sourcing is a true T*-block adjoint-weighting violation, not a crash. HONEST LEVEL: numeric (beta_eff off ~38%), reproduced via the EXACT buggy C++ path by compiling the fix commit and its parent from source -- required because the whole IFP feature is unreleased relative to v0.15.2 (the only released pre) and multi-group IFP (which the existing MG infra could drive) postdates the bug. KEY ENV FINDING: continuous-energy U235 with delayed-neutron data was generated on-box from ENDF/B-VIII.0 via NJOY (49 MB U235.h5, 6 precursor groups); single temperature (293.6 K) keeps NJOY to ~6 min; the pre/post C++ builds are incremental ninja rebuilds in the existing omc_src worktrees (the fix is C++ only -- no .py touched -- so the Python tally API is identical pre/post and only the binary differs). 'N' set-slot is the directly-evaluated NOETHER T* MR (same convention as the other entries); 'G' set-key is GenMorph (not_applicable to library bugs), distinct from the semantic G-symmetry block name.
